content: This information was last updated in August 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about the product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice and should not replace the guidance of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Common side effects of this medication may include stomach upset or pain, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, headache, muscle pain, or diarrhea. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not a comprehensive list of potential side effects. If you are in the United States or Canada and experience side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. Before taking mefloquine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, quinine, or quinidine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Mefloquine may cause dizziness or balance problems, which can be worsened by alcohol or marijuana (cannabis). Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcohol consumption. Additionally, mefloquine may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as it passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect the removal of mefloquine from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. If you are taking this medication for an extended period, laboratory and medical tests (such as eye exams and liver function tests) should be conducted regularly. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
